title: An iterative Bayesian variational quantum eigensolver with the von Mises-Fisher distribution
authors: Trung Minh Huynh, Gwangil An, Minsu Kim, Yu-Seong Jeon, Jinhyoung Lee
abstract: We develop an iterative Bayesian variational quantum eigensolver in which the unknown ground state, parametrised as a real unit vector, is inferred through a von Mises--Fisher distribution sequentially updated from   Hadamard-test measurements on a single ancilla qubit. Building on a companion paper that treated a single success outcome via exact moment matching, we generalise the scheme to condition on $m$ success outcomes for the likelihood function   per iteration. Since exact moment matching becomes impractical for $m>1$, we exploit the large-concentration regime, in which a first-order expansion of the log-likelihood yields a closed-form von Mises--Fisher   posterior with $m$ entering only through a multiplicative weight. We prove that the two convergence properties of the single-outcome scheme---non-decreasing overlap and non-decreasing concentration---are   preserved provided $m$ lies within an explicitly characterised range. Based on the theory, we propose a measurement-based algorithm and illustrate the convergence on randomly generated three- and four-qubit Hamiltonian matrices, on $\mathrm{HeH}^+$, and on $\mathrm{H}_2$.
summary: This paper introduces an iterative Bayesian VQE that estimates the ground state of a quantum Hamiltonian by modeling the state belief with a von Mises-Fisher distribution. It generalizes the measurement process to condition on multiple measurement outcomes ($m$) and rigorously proves that the estimate converges monotonically toward the true ground state while its uncertainty shrinks. This offers a theoretically grounded, measurement-based alternative to standard VQE techniques.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of finding the ground state and energy of a quantum many-body Hamiltonian using an iterative quantum algorithm.
main_result: It develops and proves the convergence of an iterative Bayesian Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) that models the state belief using a von Mises-Fisher distribution.
method: The method involves sequentially updating the belief distribution by conditioning on multiple success outcomes ($m$) from Hadamard-test measurements on an ancilla qubit.
model_or_system: The system is a general quantum many-body Hamiltonian $H$, and the state is parameterized as a real unit vector $\psi$ in the Hilbert space. The inference is performed using the von Mises-Fisher (vMF) distribution.
key_observables: Average fidelity, overlap ($R$), and concentration parameter ($\kappa$).
important_parameters: The number of success outcomes $m$, the concentration parameter $\kappa_0$, and the measurement budget $N$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-concentration regime ($\kappa_0$ large) to derive a closed-form posterior update, and the convergence theorems require $m$ to be within a specific range relative to $\kappa_0$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Hadamard test measurement scheme and show the monotonically increasing average fidelity of the algorithm on random and molecular Hamiltonians.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem and the Bayesian framework, then derives the closed-form update for the vMF posterior by generalizing moment matching for $m>1$. It mathematically proves two key convergence properties (non-decreasing overlap and concentration) and concludes with a measurement-based algorithm and numerical demonstrations.
why_interesting: This work provides a theoretically rigorous and general framework for quantum state estimation that bypasses the need for explicit circuit ansatzes, potentially offering a more robust alternative to standard gradient-based VQE methods.
